lead.headline: Fidelity files for spot Chainlink ETF as traditional finance accelerates altcoin product expansion
lead.tldr: Today's signals trace a single arc: the infrastructure of institutional crypto access is being built out asset by asset, while tokenization moves from pilot to production in Asia and political risk re-enters the US regulatory equation.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why it matters for the quarter ahead.

top_signals.title: Fidelity files for spot Chainlink ETF with planned Nasdaq listing
top_signals.summary: Fidelity has filed for a spot Chainlink (LINK) ETF to be listed on the Nasdaq exchange. The proposed fund, which would trade under the ticker FLNK, intends to hold the asset directly without staking.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Fidelity's LINK filing signals that the ETF playbook is expanding beyond BTC and ETH to liquid altcoin exposure, which reprices the timeline for institutional altcoin access and raises the bar for which assets get the wrapper next.

top_signals.title: Hyperliquid's HYPE will join bitcoin, ether and more in Franklin Templeton's crypto ETF
top_signals.summary: Franklin Templeton is adding Hyperliquid's HYPE token to its EZPZ crypto ETF. The fund will hold HYPE with roughly equal weighting alongside other major assets like Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Franklin Templeton adding HYPE to EZPZ at equal weighting to BTC and ETH is a bet on derivatives infrastructure as a core allocation, not a satellite position, which validates Hyperliquid's thesis that perpetuals DEXs deserve index inclusion.

top_signals.title: Hong Kong launches tokenized debt platform with 24-hour settlement
top_signals.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has launched a tokenized debt platform that enables 24-hour settlement across multiple currencies. The initiative aims to modernize market infrastructure with plans to potentially expand the platform to include tokenized funds.
top_signals.why_it_matters: HKMA's 24-hour multi-currency settlement platform moves tokenized debt from proof-of-concept to operational infrastructure, which means European and US issuers now face a real competitive benchmark for settlement efficiency.

top_signals.title: Japan's SBI, SMFG launch Solana joint venture for stablecoin payments and tokenization
top_signals.summary: Japan's SBI and SMFG have launched a joint venture leveraging the Solana blockchain to advance stablecoin payments and tokenization. The entity will focus on real-world asset (RWA) tokenization and on-chain asset management.
top_signals.why_it_matters: SBI and SMFG choosing Solana for their stablecoin and RWA joint venture indicates that Japanese megabanks are optimizing for throughput and cost over Ethereum's security guarantees, which has implications for how we underwrite L1 market share in institutional use cases.

top_signals.title: Senate Democrats urge SEC to scrap crypto, tokenized stock exemptions
top_signals.summary: US Democratic senators are calling on the SEC to eliminate exemptions for tokenized stocks and crypto fundraising. The move is driven by concerns over investor protections in the digital asset space.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Senate Democrats pressing SEC to roll back tokenized stock and crypto fundraising exemptions introduces tangible tail risk for US-based issuance and secondary trading infrastructure, which could accelerate geographic arbitrage toward Asia and Switzerland.

deals.company: European Union AI and quantum computing fund
deals.summary: The European Union is reportedly seeking to raise up to $55 billion to support AI and quantum computing firms. The initiative aims to decrease Europe's technological dependence on the United States and China.

on_the_radar.title: House Committee advances Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill with narrow path to passage
on_the_radar.summary: The House Committee has advanced a bill proposing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve. However, the path to final passage is narrow due to the 119th Congress adjourning in the coming weeks.

on_the_radar.title: LayerZero adds Samsung Card, Kakao Pay, ZAN as validators for upcoming Zero blockchain
on_the_radar.summary: LayerZero has onboarded Samsung Card, Kakao Pay, and ZAN as validators for its upcoming Zero blockchain. The Zero blockchain utilizes zero-knowledge proofs to decouple execution from verification, optimizing the validation process.

on_the_radar.title: Sens. Warren, Van Hollen lead push to scrap SEC's Regulation Crypto and innovation exemption
on_the_radar.summary: Senators Warren and Van Hollen are urging the SEC to scrap 'Regulation Crypto Assets' and its innovation exemption. They argue that these rules allow cryptocurrency firms to bypass essential securities laws.

on_the_radar.title: Braiins warns of Bitcoin mining attacks affecting over 1,000 sites
on_the_radar.summary: Braiins has issued a warning regarding security attacks targeting over 1,000 Bitcoin mining sites. The vulnerability stems from miners using unsecured connections, posing a systemic risk to the industry.

on_the_radar.title: Ethereum Foundation backs Keccak-256 to counter quantum, AI threats
on_the_radar.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has selected Keccak-256 to enhance the network's post-quantum security. This move is driven by the increasing threats posed by quantum computing and AI, as highlighted by Ethlabs co-founder Julian Ma.

on_the_radar.title: Ukraine passes crypto market law, with $332 million revenue target
on_the_radar.summary: Ukraine has passed a new crypto market law aimed at generating $332 million in revenue. The legislation establishes a formal tax framework for digital asset profits.

on_the_radar.title: Ukraine passes bill to legalize crypto and tax profits at 23%
on_the_radar.summary: Ukraine has passed a new bill to legalize cryptocurrency and implement a 23% tax on profits earned by individuals. The legislation also establishes a regulatory framework for the oversight of stablecoins.

on_the_radar.title: AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says
on_the_radar.summary: Computer scientist Scott Aaronson suggests that AI laboratories may have discovered undisclosed breakthroughs in cryptography. Such developments could potentially threaten the encryption standards that secure digital assets and blockchain networks.

worth_a_read.title: HyperLend Token Holder Report Q3 2026
worth_a_read.note: This report provides granular data on HyperLend's token holder concentration and staking dynamics that any investor evaluating Franklin Templeton's HYPE allocation should cross-reference against the EZPZ prospectus disclosures.

linkedin_post:
Two ETF filings in forty-eight hours. Fidelity wants Chainlink. Franklin Templeton already holds Hyperliquid's HYPE at equal weight to bitcoin and ether. The wrapper is becoming the story.

We have seen this sequence before: first the underlying asset proves liquidity, then the index provider validates it, then the passive vehicle scales it. What is different this time is speed. LINK has no futures market. HYPE is six months old. The due diligence windows are compressing, which tells us something about how issuers are competing for shelf space, not just investor dollars.

The underwriting question is whether these products pull genuine institutional allocation or just rotate existing crypto-native capital into lower-fee wrappers. We think the answer splits by asset. For LINK, the ETF is likely incremental—new money that would not self-custody. For HYPE, the equal-weighting in EZPZ reads more like a bet on derivatives exchange infrastructure as an investable theme, which is a harder sell to traditional allocators.

Asia is running a parallel experiment. Hong Kong's 24-hour settlement platform and the SBI-SMFG Solana venture are building the same institutional on-ramp without the US political overhang. The Senate Democrats' letter to the SEC, if it gains traction, does not kill tokenized stocks in the US. It just prices the regulatory premium higher and steers issuance toward jurisdictions that have already made their peace with the plumbing.

The test: whether EZPZ and FLNK see inflows in their first quarter, or whether they trade like closed-end funds at persistent discount. That gap, if it opens, is where we learn how much of this is product innovation and how much is packaging.
